theory.intro: A **composite solid** is built from simple solids. Find its volume by splitting it into parts you know, working out each part's volume, then adding or subtracting them.
facts: Split the solid into named simple parts and find each part's volume with its own formula.
Cone $V = \frac{1}{3}\pi r^{2}h$; cylinder $V = \pi r^{2}h$; sphere $V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^{3}$; hemisphere $V = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$; pyramid $V = \frac{1}{3}Ah$.
Two hemispheres of the same radius together make one whole sphere.
Keep each part's volume **unrounded** and round only the final total, so no rounding error builds up.
For capacity, convert the total: $1$ cm³ $= 1$ mL, $1000$ cm³ $= 1$ L, $1$ m³ $= 1000$ L.
steps: Split the composite solid into simple solids
Find the volume of each simple solid

development.question_text: An ice-cream is a cone of radius $2.5$ cm and height $10$ cm, topped with a hemisphere of the same radius. Find its total capacity in millilitres, to the nearest mL. ($1$ cm³ $= 1$ mL)

A capsule-shaped tank is a cylinder of radius $0.5$ m and height $2$ m with a hemisphere on each end (together a full sphere). Find its capacity in litres, correct to $1$ decimal place. ($1$ m³ $= 1000$ L)

mastery.question_text: A square-based pyramid sits exactly on top of a cube to form a solid. The cube has an edge of $5$ m and the pyramid has a perpendicular height of $9$ m. Find the total volume of the solid in m³.
An ice-cream is a cone of radius $3$ cm topped with a hemisphere of the same radius. Its total volume is $45\pi$ cm³. Find the perpendicular height of the cone, in cm.
mastery.solution_text:
$V_{\text{hemisphere}} = \frac{2}{3}\pi r^{3}$
$= \frac{2}{3} \times \pi \times 3^{3}$
$= 18\pi$
$V_{\text{cone}} = \frac{1}{3}\pi \times 3^{2} \times h = 3\pi h$
$V_{\text{total}} = 18\pi + 3\pi h$
$45\pi = 18\pi + 3\pi h$
$27\pi = 3\pi h$
$h = 9\text{ cm}$

mastery.question_text: A grain silo is a cylinder of radius $2$ m and height $5$ m, topped by a cone of the same radius and height $1.5$ m. Find its capacity in litres, to the nearest litre. ($1$ m³ $= 1000$ L)
